A small shadcn-style UI library sub-component that renders a pagination ellipsis span with an icon. It is a reusable presentational component, but minor and part of a larger pagination component set. It has no callers, so its significance is low.

Generated OpenAPI client SDK method (sdk.gen.ts) that wraps a POST to /api/v1/private/users/. It is generated boilerplate mirroring an API operation defined elsewhere, so it is not an architectural element on its own. It does make an HTTP call to the backend, which counts as external integration.

TanStack Router module augmentation boilerplate declaring the router type for type-safety. Not executable behavior or a meaningful architectural element; pure TypeScript type registration scaffolding.

This is a TanStack Router type map generated in routeTree.gen.ts. Generated code is excluded from architectural modelling. The routes it lists would be modelled from their source route files, not from this type-level index, which has no callers or behaviour.

This is the HTTP route handler for POST /password-recovery/{email}, so it is an API operation. It drives credential recovery by issuing a password-reset token, an authentication concern, and returns a uniform response to prevent email enumeration. The database read and email sending happen in the callees it invokes, not in the handler itself.

React dialog-form component for editing an item, embedded in a dropdown menu. It is non-routable, renders the UI, validates input with zod and calls the generated API client to update the item. It is a notable UI fragment within the items feature, but it is not a routable view.

A shadcn/Radix wrapper that styles a dropdown checkbox item, making it a reusable UI library component. It is a thin, generated-style primitive with no callers, so its architectural significance is minor. It renders UI and implements no other concern.

POST /items route handler is an API operation exposing item creation. It persists the new Item via the DB session, setting owner_id from the current user. Authentication is resolved by the CurrentUser dependency, not by the handler itself, and no permission check occurs here.

A small React hook that wraps the sonner toast library to show standardised success and error notifications. It is a reusable UI feedback pattern, but it is a thin wrapper of minor architectural weight.

POST /test-email/ is an HTTP API operation that generates a test email and sends it through the email service, an external SMTP integration. It is a utility or admin endpoint, so it is notable but not core. The route itself does no authentication; any superuser dependency is applied elsewhere.

A reusable shadcn-style UI library component that renders a responsive sidebar. It switches to a mobile sheet and supports variant and collapsible modes. It is consumed by AppSidebar and is notable within the UI kit, but it is generic scaffolding rather than an application-specific view.

SQLModel base schema defining shared Item properties (title, description) with validation constraints. It is a non-table base class used by Item DTOs and the table model. It is a logical data-model object schema with moderate significance and does no persistence work itself.

A trivial props interface for a sidebar React component that declares only an items array. It is type boilerplate for the component rather than an architectural element, so it is classed as an implementation detail.

A small Pydantic settings validator that rewrites the Postgres DSN scheme so it uses the psycopg driver. It is a configuration normalization helper, does not itself access the database, and is too low-level to record as an architecture element.

A shadcn-style thin wrapper around the Radix Tooltip Provider that sets a default delay. It is a reusable UI library component, but it is trivial boilerplate used only within the UI kit (by Tooltip and SidebarProvider), so its architectural significance is minimal.

A shadcn-style sidebar primitive that renders a styled button (or a Slot) for group-level actions. It is a small reusable UI action element inside a generated component library, with no callers. That makes it a low-significance UX action component.

Handler for the PATCH /users/{user_id} route, making it an API operation. It loads the user through the DB session, checks email uniqueness, and updates the record, so it does persistence work itself. Any superuser authorization dependency sits in the decorator, not in this function body.

A trivial shadcn/ui wrapper that passes props through to the Radix Sheet Trigger and adds a data-slot attribute. It is generated-style UI boilerplate with no logic. It belongs to the Sheet library component rather than standing as its own architectural element.

A trivial React props interface containing only a children field for the AuthLayout component. It is boilerplate typing, not an architectural element in its own right; the AuthLayout component itself would be the modelled UX element.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts utility module that serializes query key values into JSON-friendly shapes for Pinia Colada caching. It is generated boilerplate made of pure formatting helpers, with no architectural role of its own.

Generated OpenAPI SDK client method wrapping PATCH /api/v1/users/{user_id}. It is generated boilerplate mirroring the backend API contract, so it is not an architectural element on its own. It does perform an outbound HTTP call to the backend, which counts as external integration.

A shadcn/ui-style styled wrapper around Radix DropdownMenu SubContent. It is a reusable UI library primitive that applies class names and passes props through. It renders UI, but it is generated-style boilerplate with no callers, so its architectural significance is minor.

Generated OpenAPI client SDK method (sdk.gen.ts) wrapping a PATCH to /api/v1/users/me. Generated code is not recorded as an architecture element on its own; the underlying API operation lives on the backend. It does perform an outbound HTTP call, so external_integration applies. The bearer security metadata is declarative only, not authentication logic.

Generated TanStack Router type declaration in routeTree.gen.ts that enumerates route paths and IDs for type safety. It is generated boilerplate. The routes themselves would be modelled in the navigation layer, but this typing interface is not an architectural element on its own.

A trivial computed property on the Settings config class. It checks whether the SMTP host and from-address are both set. It is a configuration helper with no behaviour of its own, so it is not architecturally meaningful as a standalone element.

ItemsPublic is a SQLModel DTO that defines the paginated list response shape (data plus count) returned by the read_items route. It is a non-table schema, so it belongs in the data model as an object schema. It is a notable response contract but structurally simple.

Core security module defining JWT access token creation (HS256 with secret key), and password hashing/verification using Argon2/Bcrypt. It establishes the application's authentication mechanism and credential policy, so it maps to an AuthenticationConfig in the security layer. It is architecturally significant but small.

A TanStack file route module defining the routable /signup page: a sign-up form view with zod validation, a redirect for logged-in users, and submission via the signUp mutation. It is primarily a user-facing view, a key entry point for account registration, and part of the authentication flow.

POST route operation that previews password recovery email HTML. It looks up the user via a DB session and generates a reset token, so it touches authentication and persistence. It is a secondary admin/debug endpoint (in the FastAPI template it is superuser-guarded via a dependency), so its significance is moderate.

A small props interface for the Logo UI component. It only declares the component's input shape (variant, className, asLink) and is an implementation detail of that component. It is not an architectural element in its own right; the Logo component itself would be the modelled UX element.

Pydantic request body model defined inline in the private routes module, describing the payload for a private user-creation endpoint. It is an API-local request schema rather than a canonical domain entity. It is minor and has no behaviour; it only carries a password field without verifying credentials.

POST /reset-password/ is an HTTP API operation. It verifies a password-reset token, which is credential handling and so counts as authentication. It updates the user's password in the database, so it persists data. As a public security-sensitive endpoint, it is architecturally significant.

File-based route module defining the routable Password Recovery page: form view with zod validation, calls the LoginService recover-password API, and has a beforeLoad guard redirecting logged-in users. It is primarily a routable UI view and participates in the credential recovery flow.

FastAPI router module grouping the /utils endpoints (test-email, health-check). It forms part of the API surface but is a minor utility group. Authorization and email sending are delegated to dependencies and helpers, so the module itself implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Generated OpenAPI client SDK method (sdk.gen.ts) wrapping GET /api/v1/users/me with a bearer security hint. Because it is generated code, it is not modelled on its own; the API operation it targets is the architectural element. It does make the HTTP call to the backend, so external integration applies.

Thin wrapper that opens a database session and delegates seeding to init_db. It is bootstrap scaffolding with no logic of its own. Persistence is performed by the callee, not by this function, so no concern is flagged.

POST /signup is a public HTTP API operation for self-registration. It creates user credentials (identity onboarding) and persists the new user via CRUD calls. It is a significant system-boundary endpoint, though not a core architectural abstraction.

Auto-generated type declarations from @hey-api/openapi-ts for the Axios HTTP client config and request options. Generated boilerplate with only type definitions and no behaviour; not an architecturally meaningful element on its own.

FastAPI router module defining the /private API surface with a POST /private/users/ endpoint that creates users directly. It is a development-only API grouping, so it sits in the api layer. It persists via the session. Password hashing is delegated to a callee, so authentication is not marked.

A build-time configuration file for the hey-api OpenAPI client code generator. It specifies the input spec, the output directory and the plugins used. It is a tooling artifact rather than runtime behaviour, and has minor significance as the source of the generated API client.

Generated OpenAPI client SDK method wrapping GET /api/v1/users/. It is generated code, a thin HTTP client call. The API operation itself would be modelled from the backend route, so this is not a separate architectural element. It does perform an outbound HTTP call, which counts as external integration.

A shadcn/ui-style reusable Badge presentational component with style variants. It is a generic UI library primitive, so it maps to a ux librarycomponent of low architectural significance. It renders UI and has no other cross-cutting concerns.

A props type for the DeleteUser React component, holding only an id and an onSuccess callback. It is an implementation detail of that component's signature, not a standalone architectural element. The component itself would be modelled in the ux layer.

Routable password-recovery page component rendering a form and calling the backend recovery API. It is a UX view within the authentication flow. It drives credential-recovery behaviour and calls the backend via the generated client, but it is a single screen of moderate significance.

The module defines the application's database engine, a central persistence connection built from DATABASE_URL. It also provides init_db, which seeds the first superuser into the database. It is the physical data store entry point, so it is modelled as the database element and is architecturally significant.

A shadcn-style UI primitive that renders a styled span for keyboard shortcut hints in dropdown menus. It is a reusable library component, but trivial, generated-style boilerplate with no callers, so its architectural significance is minimal. It renders UI.

This module is auto-generated by @hey-api/openapi-ts. It holds client utility helpers: query serialization, auth parameter injection and URL building. Generated scaffolding of this kind is not an architecturally meaningful element on its own. The generated API client as a whole would be modelled instead, if at all.

A React skeleton loading placeholder for the users table. It is a small UI component rendering a pending/loading state from table and skeleton primitives. It is user-facing but has minor architectural significance.

An HTTP POST route that validates the bearer access token via the CurrentUser dependency and returns the authenticated user. It is part of the API surface and is authentication-focused, but it is a minor diagnostic endpoint, so significance is moderate.

A shadcn-style reusable sidebar UI component library module: provider, context hook and composable sidebar parts. It is a reusable UI component definition in the ux layer. The cookie it writes for open/closed state is a trivial UI preference, not durable persistence. It is generated or vendored-style UI scaffolding, so its significance is moderate.

Vite build configuration file defining the frontend build pipeline (React SWC, TanStack router codegen, Tailwind) and its output into the backend's static directory. It is a build/deployment configuration artifact in the technology layer, and notable because it couples the frontend bundle to the backend deployment.

React component rendering the sidebar user menu dropdown with settings link and logout action. It is a non-routable UI fragment embedded in AppSidebar. It calls useAuth's logout but does not implement authentication itself. Its role is primarily rendering the UI.

Root route component of the TanStack Router tree, rendering the Outlet that hosts all child routes plus devtools. It acts as the root of the app's navigation structure, so it belongs in the navigation layer as a route, and it renders UI.

HTTP route handler for POST /login/test-token that validates the bearer token through the CurrentUser dependency and returns the authenticated user. It is a small but public API operation on the authentication surface, not a test suite despite its name.

This is a trivial inner wrapper inside the useCustomToast hook that calls toast.success with a fixed title. It is widely used but has no architectural weight of its own. It does drive user-facing UI feedback, so user_interface is true. The enclosing hook, not this function, would be the element worth modelling.

The CRUD module is the persistence access layer for the User and Item tables, covering create, update and query operations through SQLModel sessions. It also implements credential authentication, using password verification with timing-attack protection and hash upgrades. This makes it a central data-access unit of the backend.

This is standard Alembic env.py scaffolding that emits offline migration SQL to script output. It is generated boilerplate, not a distinct architectural element; the migrations themselves would be modelled in data-store. It does not touch a database directly, since offline mode needs no DBAPI.

Central application configuration loaded from environment/.env via pydantic BaseSettings: database DSN, SMTP, Sentry, secret key, token expiry. It is a deployment configuration artifact shared across the backend rather than business logic. Reading the .env file is configuration loading, not durable data persistence. It validates secrets but performs no authentication itself.

Generated OpenAPI client SDK method wrapping DELETE /api/v1/items/{id}. Generated code is boilerplate; the API operation itself is modelled on the backend. It does perform an HTTP call to the backend, so external_integration applies, but it only declares the bearer scheme rather than performing authentication.

A props type for a shadcn-style loading button component. It is a type-level detail of a UI library component rather than an architectural element itself. It is minor and pertains to the UI, but the component, not this interface, would be what gets modelled.

SQLModel DTO defining the optional-field shape for user update payloads, with validation constraints on email, name and password length. It is a non-table schema (the data shape for an API request), so it belongs in the data model as an object schema of moderate significance.
